extraContext:
# Issue #1: Codex rate-limit awareness via app-server

## Problem

`vibe` waits out Claude rate limits (`budget.waitOnRateLimit`, `withRateLimitRetry` in `src/orchestrator.ts`) but is completely blind to Codex's. On a subscription the rate-limit window — not cost — is the thing that actually stops a long unattended run, so this is the one brake with no Codex-side equivalent.

## What is available

`codex app-server` (experimental JSON-RPC over stdio) answers `account/rateLimits/read`. Measured response on a ChatGPT Plus account:

```json
{
  "rateLimits": {
    "limitId": "codex",
    "primary": { "usedPercent": 15, "windowDurationMins": 10080, "resetsAt": 1787196925 },
    "secondary": null,
    "credits": { "hasCredits": true, "unlimited": false, "balance": "974.5723860000" },
    "spendControlReached": false,
    "planType": "plus"
  }
}
```

There is also an `AccountRateLimitsUpdatedNotification` ("sparse rolling rate-limit update") in the protocol schema, so a client that holds the connection open gets pushed updates rather than having to poll.

Handshake: `initialize` with a `clientInfo` object, then an `initialized` notification, then calls. Omitting `clientInfo` fails every subsequent call with `-32600 Not initialized`.

## Proposed behaviour

- Read `usedPercent` before an expensive Codex turn; if it is above a configurable threshold, stop the run resumably rather than starting work that will fail partway.
- On `rateLimitReachedType` being non-null, wait until `resetsAt` under the existing `budget.maxWaitMinutes` cap, reusing the wait/escalate logic Claude already has.
- Surface `usedPercent` in the run summary alongside the token totals.

## Risks

- `app-server` is marked **experimental** and the protocol is versioned (`v1`/`v2` schema dirs). This is a stability bet in a way `codex exec --json` is not.
- It is a second process model — a persistent stdio JSON-RPC connection alongside the existing one-shot `codex exec` spawns.
- `usedPercent` is an integer percent of a rolling window (10080 min = weekly here). It does not move measurably for a single turn, so it is a coarse whole-run brake, not per-turn metering.

## Not a solution to

Cost accounting. See the "Notes and limitations" section of the README: no endpoint returns money, and `credits.balance` was measured not to move when subscription-metered work is done.


---

# Working constraints for this task

## Tests are part of the deliverable

This repo currently has no test suite and no `test` script. As part of this
change:

- Add tests covering the new code, especially the JSON-RPC framing and the
  parsing of the rate-limit payload. Those are pure functions over strings and
  objects and can be tested without spawning anything.
- Add an npm `test` script so `npm test` runs them. Use the Node built-in test
  runner; there are no test dependencies today and adding a framework is not
  required.
- Make whatever build/config changes that needs (tsconfig currently includes
  only `src/**/*.ts`).
- Do not spawn a real `codex app-server` from a test. It requires a logged-in
  account, takes seconds, and hits the network. Structure the code so the
  transport is separable from the parsing, and test the parsing.

The verification command for this run is:

    npm run typecheck && npm run build && npm test

All three must pass. `npm test` currently fails with "Missing script", so the
task is not complete until that script exists and passes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the `codex exec --json` path in `src/codex.ts` that ordinary
  turns depend on. This is additive.
- Match the existing code's commenting style: comments explain why a decision
  was made, usually citing the concrete failure that motivated it. Do not add
  comments that restate what the line does.
- The codebase is strict TypeScript with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and
  `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, and there is no `any` in the source. Keep it
  that way.
- Internal imports use the `@src/*` alias, not relative `../..` chains.
- `app-server` is experimental. If it is unavailable or the handshake fails,
  the run must continue unaffected rather than dying - this is an optional
  signal, never a new failure mode.
